question:
(i) Explain why a capacitor offers opposition to alternating current and define capacitive reactance.
(ii) A capacitor of capacitance $40\,\mu\text{F}$ is connected to an AC source of frequency $50\,\text{Hz}$. Calculate its capacitive reactance. Take $\pi = 3.14$.
(iii) How will this reactance change if the frequency is doubled? Justify your answer.

options.A:
(i) Capacitive reactance is opposition due to an inductor and $X_C=2\pi fC$.
(ii) $X_C=159.2\,\Omega$.
(iii) Doubling frequency doubles $X_C$.
options.B:
(i) Capacitive reactance is resistance of the dielectric and is independent of frequency.
(ii) $X_C=40\,\Omega$.
(iii) Doubling frequency leaves it unchanged.
options.C:
(i) A capacitor blocks AC completely.
(ii) $X_C=79.6\,\Omega$.
(iii) Doubling frequency makes $X_C$ four times.
options.D:
(i) A capacitor offers opposition to AC during repeated charging and discharging; this opposition is $X_C=\frac{1}{\omega C}=\frac{1}{2\pi fC}$.
(ii) For $C=40\,\mu\text{F}$ and $f=50\,\text{Hz}$, $X_C\approx79.6\,\Omega$.
(iii) Since $X_C\propto\frac{1}{f}$, doubling frequency makes $X_C$ half.
